roster.autonomy_quote: This isn't a test—this is what autonomous robots in production operations look like
autonomously transferring totes from autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) to conveyors
autonomously planned its path and adjusted or paused work around people and obstacles
autonomously checks harness connection status and reports anomalies
autonomously picked totes from a storage stack, transported them to a conveyor and placed them at a pickup point for human operators
serving real production workflows with zero teleoperation and autonomously
autonomously identifying incoming cells and planning grasp paths
autonomously pick up tablets, navigate the factory, place devices into test fixtures and sort finished or defective units
autonomously performing industrial material loading and tray handling alongside humans
autonomously identifying shelves, picking medicines, checking them visually, packing them and placing them into pickup lockers 'without human intervention'
autonomously completing 10+ consecutive actions per cycle to fetch, transfer and load small parts onto loading stations in under 40 seconds with no human teleoperation

Autonomy and real parcel output qualify, but R1 explicitly requires ability to move itself between workstations. The cited Sina article documents grasping/flipping, not self-locomotion; the cited Economic Observer follow-up describes a column lower body, with no lower-limb components, cheaper than wheeled robots. No self-moving base is documented. R1's parenthetical inclusion of column-based humanoids conflicts with its self-mobility condition here; applying the explicit AND condition conservatively excludes this pair.

Opened the cited Economic Observer source: '下半身是立柱，不需要下肢的结构及核心零部件' and '也比轮式机器人更便宜'. Column lower body and station-bound parcel handling do not document the self-mobility R1 explicitly requires. The claim also does not explicitly state autonomous work (R3). If column-based humanoids are intended to bypass mobility, the May 15 record would establish one China Post pair, not a second Shenzhen case.
Explicitly sensing-only autonomous inspections, with no manipulation or repair.
